text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Presidents Mubarak and Assad said comprehensive and just peace must be based on the pirnciple of land for peace. Mubarak, after talks with Assad in Damascus, says that settlements are the gravest obstacle the Palestinians face and that if they continue they will complicate the final status negotiations.

- The ministerial working group on developing the area south of Hurghada, at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri yesterday, discussed the biggest tourist project in the area. Ali Nigm of Delta International Bank said the project would cost up to $10 billion.

- Ministers of water resources from the nine Nile Basin countries agreed that Egypt would provide facilities for training people on water resource management. They also agreed on a new framework for the Nile Basin states through setting up a new mechanism to enable the states to manage the river.
- Mubarak and Assad held a summit in Damascus amd discuss the possibility of resuming megotiations on the Syrian track.
- President Hosni Mubarak will have important talks with the president of Tataristan today. Businessmen accompanying him will discuss increasing investment and trade.
- The general secretariat of the ruling National Democratic Party has finished reviewing the lists of candidates for local council elections. The lists will be sent to local branches.

- The secretariat of the trade unions federation has finished drafting a law on voluntary early retirement for public-sector workers. It suggests minimum compensation of 15,000 pounds ($4,400), up to a maximum of 35,000 pounds.
- EgyptAir will lay on 260 extra flights from March 23 to carry 55,000 pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.
